BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL  ON THE 16 th OF APRIL, 2024  CRIMINAL APPEAL No. 11550 of 2023  BETWEEN:-
 GURU PRASAD TIWARI S/O HRIDAYAL TIWARI, AGED  ABOUT 51 YEARS, OCCUPATION: LABOUR R/O VILLAGE  BHIR P.S. MANGAWA DISTT. REWA (MADHYA  PRADESH)
 
 (BY SHRI MANISH DATT - SENIOR ADVOCATE WITH SHRI D.S.DUBEY -  ADVOCATE)

AND  1. THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH THROUGH  POLICE STATION MANGAWA DISTRICT REWA  (MADHYA PRADESH)
 2. VICTIM X D/O

NOT MENTION THROUGH P.S.
 MANGAWA DISTRICT (MADHYA PRADESH)

(BY SHRI S.K.MALVI - PANEL LAWYER FOR RESPONDENT NO.1/STATE  AND SHRI ANIL KUMAR YADAV - ADVOCATE FOR OBJECTOR)
 This appeal coming on for admission this day, th e cour  following:
 ORDER

This second application for grant of bail in the form of criminal appeal under Section 14-A of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 has been filed assailing the order dated 01.09.2023 passed by learned Special Judge, SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, District Rewa (M.P.), whereby application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.
for grant of regular bail filed on behalf of appellant/accused has been dismissed.

sentences.text: 2. Appellant has been arrested in connection with F.I.R. bearing Crime No.564/2022 dated 20.10.2022 registered at Police Station-Mangawa, District- Rewa (M.P.) for commission of offence under Sections 376, 306 of IPC and Section 3(2)(v) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.

sentences.text: Appellant/accused is in detention since 23.10.2022.

3. Appellant's first application was dismissed as withdrawn and not pressed vide order dated 27.02.2023 passed in Cr.A.No.2208/2023 with liberty to renew the prayer for bail after evidence of complainant Mithailal before the trial court.

4. As per the prosecution story which emerges from the statement of Mithailal Saket is that on 09.10.2022 at around 11 A.M. he had gone to take irrigation pipe from Tejmani Sharma's agriculture field situated at Ahri as he had taken that agricultural field from Tejmani on share out.
It is alleged that when he was returning after taking pipe, his daughter-in-law Maya Saket was cutting grass in the agricultural field of Guru Prasad Tiwari.
Guru Prasad Tiwari was sitting on the boundary of the field.
He ate betel nut and clove with Guru Prasad Tiwari.
Guru Prasad Tiwari had asked his daughter-in-law to cut fodder for animals.
Thereafter, they both proceeded towards Guru Prasad Tiwari's agricultural field.
After sometime when he came, he heard some noise.
Hearing noise when he reached near babool tree, he found Guru Prasad Tiwari committing rape/ sex upon her daughter-in-law.
He had told Guru Prasad Tiwari whether he use to call daughters and sisters for said purpose only.
Guru Prasad Tiwari pushed him and fled away.
After coming to home he narrated the entire story to his wife and daughter.
Thereafter, they all went in search of his daughter-in-law but she could not be traced.
At around 9 P.M. when he was going to lodge F.I.R, Guru Prasad Tiwari met on the way and told that he will get his F.I.R lodged.
In police outpost, policeman gave a paper and on it Guru Prasad Tiwari wrote something and handed over to the police.
When he gave the copy of that report to his son, he informed that it is only missing report.
It is further alleged that he had give a complaint to Superintendent of Police on 18.10.2022.
On 20.10.2022, his daughter-in-law's dead body was found hanging with branch of Mango tree.
Guru Prasad Tiwari with an intention to screen the evidence after committing rape has murdered his daughter-in-law.
After investigation charge sheet has been filed.
5. Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that the appellant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
The entire prosecution story has been prepared.
The same is false and concocted.
In the postmortem report death of deceased has been found due to hanging.
It is not a case of murder.
It is further submitted that DNA report has been received and it does not confirm the factum of rape/ sex with the deceased.
There is no eye witness account except the evidence of Mithailal Saket who has lodged the missing report almost after 8-9 days of the alleged incident.
It is further submitted that Mithailal Saket has already been examined before the trial court.
Now, there is no possibility of influencing of the prosecution witnesses and tempering with the prosecution evidence.
Applicant is in jail for last 20 months.
Final conclusion of the trial will take considerable time.
Therefore, it is prayed that appellant may be released on bail by setting aside the impugned order.

6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State as well as counsel for the objector have opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the appellant and have submitted that it is a case in which truth has Guru Prasad Tiwari vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188546146/
2 been deliberately manipulated by the present applicant in collusion with the police of the concerned police station.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Mithailal Saket had gone to lodge F.I.R but police instead of writing his report gave the paper to the accused who made a mention about missing of daughter-in-law.
Police did not wrote F.I.R as per his saying.
It is further submitted that Mithailal Saket had seen present appellant committing rape upon deceased.
Present appellant in collusion with the police has deliberately concealed.
It is contended that appellant has criminal background of three cases.
7. In this case, after investigation charge sheet has already been filed.
Mithailal Saket has already been examined before the trial Court.
As per postmortem report, death of the deceased was due to asphyxia.
DNA report does not confirm sexual act.

Therefore, having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case including the material on record, but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pre-trial detention of the appellant is not warranted.

Consequently, this appeal under Section 14-A of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 stands allowed and the impugned order dated 01.09.2023 passed by learned 12th Addl. Sessions Judge and Special Judge, SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, District Rewa is set- aside.

sentences.text: 8. It is directed that appellant - Guru Prasad Tiwari be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
9.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case o f bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.
